items.title: $AAPL Bank of America flagged a new kind of Apple risk on Tuesday, and it isn't the iPhone. Analyst Wamsi Mohan's note: Meta's M
items.content_excerpt: $AAPL Bank of America flagged a new kind of Apple risk on Tuesday, and it isn't the iPhone. Analyst Wamsi Mohan's note: Meta's Muse agent could reroute product discovery and transactions around the app store entirely. His line: "The risk for Apple is that it can keep every handset sale and still lose discovery, referral, and transaction initiation." The adoption numbers give the note teeth. Muse launched Sept 8 and hit about 2.5 million downloads in its first two weeks, per BofA, topping the US iOS free chart. Shopify, Expedia and PayPal have plugged in commerce rails. Amazon blocked it. Apple shipped a rebuilt Siri with iOS 27 on Sept 14, but Mohan says it lacks Muse-style persistent background actions and a comparable payment rail. Apple fell 2.7% on Tuesday. Meta rose 3.2%. BofA kept a Buy and a 370 target anyway. Tracking whether Muse's commerce partners start reporting transaction volumes.

items.title: Just weeks into his tenure as Apple’s CEO, John Ternus is reportedly leading a major structural overhaul aimed at accelerating product devel
items.content_excerpt: Just weeks into his tenure as Apple’s CEO, John Ternus is reportedly leading a major structural overhaul aimed at accelerating product development, expanding the company’s device ecosystem and creating a leaner organization, according to Bloomberg News. The former head of hardware is seeking to reduce layers of middle management and shorten the distance between senior executives and engineers. Ternus has reportedly told colleagues that a more experimental and dynamic culture is essential for Apple to compete in the artificial-intelligence era. As part of the restructuring, Ternus is also considering moving away from Apple’s traditional spring and fall product-launch cycles in favor of a more flexible and frequent release schedule that could bring new products and features to market faster. The changes are unfolding alongside broader cost-cutting efforts. With growth in Apple’s high-margin services business slowing. $AAPL

items.title: Amazon Prime Video International VP Kelly Day defended the use of AI in entertainment, saying the technology is already reducing production
items.content_excerpt: Amazon Prime Video International VP Kelly Day defended the use of AI in entertainment, saying the technology is already reducing production costs without sacrificing quality. Speaking at the Royal Television Society convention in London, Day said AI can allow Prime Video to tell more stories, take greater creative risks and give more diverse perspectives a platform. Day stressed that Amazon is not seeking to replace creative talent with AI, but rather reduce administrative work so creators can focus on their creative vision. Prime Video has already used AI for dubbing some series, including in Latin America, where the practice has drawn criticism from viewers and dubbing professionals. A CVL Economics study estimates AI could affect 118,500 U.S. jobs in film, television and animation in 2026 as some tasks are consolidated, replaced or eliminated. Day also said ethical principles for AI use must be established from the outset. $AMZN

items.title: Jim Cramer said Wall Street may be overreacting to the threat posed by Meta’s Muse AI agent to consumer companies, creating potential opport
items.content_excerpt: Jim Cramer said Wall Street may be overreacting to the threat posed by Meta’s Muse AI agent to consumer companies, creating potential opportunities among stocks that have been broadly sold off. The so-called “consumer inertia” trade assumes AI agents could hurt businesses that benefit when customers fail to cancel subscriptions, compare prices or shop around for better deals. Since Muse launched Sept. 8, Planet Fitness has fallen 20%, while Airbnb and Booking Holdings are down 13% and 16%, respectively. SiriusXM has dropped about 11%, Charles Schwab 9% and Life Time 7%. Cramer argued that investors should assess each company’s actual exposure to AI rather than treating entire industries as potential losers. He pointed to Life Time as an example, saying its highly engaged members may be less likely to cancel than Planet Fitness customers. In travel, Cramer said online agencies retain value through features such as rewards programs and easy price comparisons. $META

items.title: Google has been paying about 100 digital publishers for content used in AI-powered answers across its search engine and other products, The
items.content_excerpt: Google has been paying about 100 digital publishers for content used in AI-powered answers across its search engine and other products, The Information reported Tuesday, citing people familiar with the matter. The pilot program marks a shift from Google’s traditional position that it should not pay publishers whose content helps answer user queries, arguing that search traffic directs users to their websites and provides economic value. However, the rollout of AI-generated summaries, known as AI Overviews, has significantly reduced the amount of traffic Google sends to publishers’ sites. The change has triggered widespread complaints and lawsuits from some publishers, who argue that Google is benefiting from their content while reducing the traffic that supports their businesses. The payments could signal a new approach as Google faces growing pressure over how digital content is used to power AI features and how publishers are compensated. $GOOGL $GOOG

items.content_excerpt: President Donald Trump released the seating chart for Tuesday’s “Super Intelligence Luncheon” at the White House, highlighting the concentration of political and corporate leaders around the AI industry. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang sat beside Trump, with Elon Musk on the other side, while Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg was nearby and Vice President JD Vance opposite. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei sat near Broadcom CEO Hock Tan, while OpenAI president Greg Brockman was seated near Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick. Another group included Palantir CEO Alex Karp, White House technology adviser Michael Kratsios and FTC Chairman Andrew Ferguson. Google CEO Sundar Pichai and executives from AMD, Micron, ServiceNow and Palo Alto Networks also attended. The gathering brought together AI-model developers, chipmakers, infrastructure providers, technology platforms, investors and government officials. $NVDA $TSLA $META $PLTR

items.content_excerpt: This is one of the more interesting $SOFI takes I’ve seen recently. Patient Capital Management owns more than 1.5M shares of SoFi and increased its position last quarter. In a response shared by a SoFi investor today, Patient Capital said it believes SoFi is still in the early innings of an inflection in Financial Services fee monetization. But this was the part that caught my attention: They view Galileo as essentially a “free call option” because they believe SoFi’s current valuation prices in little, if any, value for the Tech Platform. If the core business keeps growing while Galileo, the Loan Platform Business and SoFiUSD start contributing meaningful returns, that optionality starts getting really interesting.

That’s when the fun begins.

items.content_excerpt: $CAPR Capricor's late-breaking WMS poster has the number behind tonight's ~20% after-hours pop. Patients who switched from placebo to deramiocel in HOPE-3 slowed upper-limb decline 76% vs their own prior year on placebo (PUL 2.0 scale: 2.05 points down to 0.49). Elbow-related function slowed 66% (1.33 to 0.45). Same patients, two different years: year 1 on placebo is the control for year 2 on drug. The group on drug from the start read almost identical across both years (0.95 vs 0.89 points). Both groups beat the natural-history model over two years (3.42 vs 5.88 predicted for the early group; 3.76 vs 5.35 for switchers). This data is already inside the BLA. Capricor filed the 24-month cut as a major amendment after July's adcomm, pushing the PDUFA to November 22. B. Riley is Buy / $21 PT (from $5) with a 40% approval probability. Stock closed at $8.57, down 70% YTD. Saturday's follow-up WMS presentation covers muscle and cardiac efficacy.

Charts don’t see that. All my opinion and anything is possible.

items.title: $VNDA Vanda's Phase III readout for Hetlioz in delayed sleep-wake phase disorder hit this morning: sleep onset moved 42.5 minutes earlie
items.content_excerpt: $VNDA Vanda's Phase III readout for Hetlioz in delayed sleep-wake phase disorder hit this morning: sleep onset moved 42.5 minutes earlier on drug vs 5.4 on placebo, a 37.1-minute difference (p=0.022). Responder rate: 60% advanced at least 30 minutes vs 15% on placebo. This is a label expansion, not a new molecule, which matters for two reasons. One: the sNDA rides on an already-approved drug with a known safety profile. Two: the population math. Hetlioz's current indications are rare ones. Vanda puts DSWPD prevalence at 0.5 to 4.1 million US adults. If approved, it would be the first FDA-approved medicine for the condition. Keep the small print in view: 43 patients enrolled over five-plus years, 40 in the efficacy analysis, and the endpoint was a sleep diary. Vanda will discuss the data with FDA before filing the sNDA.

items.content_excerpt: $GT J. C. Penney Company, Inc. and its affiliated debtors filed chapter 11 petitions on May 15, 2020 in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Southern District of Texas (Corpus Christi Division), case number 20-20182, before Hon. David R. Jones. The filing arrived after the company closed all 846 of its stores under COVID-19 lockdowns and lost the operating cash flow needed to service roughly $5 billion in funded debt. JCPenney entered the case with a Restructuring Support Agreement already in hand from its first lien ad hoc group, contemplating a sale to lenders rather than a stand-alone reorganization. Shareholders got nothing.

items.content_excerpt: $SPY $DJT $QQQ $VOO $VTI Fed's Williams Sees No Urgency For Next Rate Hike Reuters Yields were choppy on this earlier. New York Fed President John Williams said Tuesday the central bank has time to weigh incoming data before deciding when to raise rates again after September's quarter-point move to a 3.75%–4% target range. "With the policy action we took at our September meeting, there is no need for urgency," he said at the University at Buffalo. If the economy tracks his forecast, he said one further upward adjustment late this year may be appropriate. CME FedWatch showed October hike odds falling to about 51.5% after his remarks, from nearly 70% earlier in the session.

items.title: What the heck happened to $FICO ? 👀 Down -27% today, marking its worst single day decline since 1989. Shares are now down more than 70% from
items.content_excerpt: What the heck happened to $FICO ? 👀 Down -27% today, marking its worst single day decline since 1989. Shares are now down more than 70% from the November 2024 intra day high of $2,402.40. That is an absolutely brutal collapse for a company that was once viewed as having a dominant position in credit scoring. 🔹The major catalyst is a change in the mortgage credit scoring landscape. The FHFA announced that Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac will move to a single pricing grid, with VantageScore joining the existing FICO Classic scoring system. That means VantageScore can now compete directly with FICO in mortgage lending, potentially reducing FICO’s role and pricing power. 🔹Then Rocket Mortgage announced it plans to make VantageScore 4.0 its preferred scoring model for eligible mortgages in Q4. Investors are now repricing FICO around the possibility of increased competition and lower demand for its scores in the mortgage market. $SPY $QQQ $IWM $DIA

items.title: JPMorgan Chase & Co. has hired three senior bankers to strengthen its natural-resources investment banking team, according to a memo rev
items.content_excerpt: JPMorgan Chase & Co. has hired three senior bankers to strengthen its natural-resources investment banking team, according to a memo reviewed by Bloomberg News. David Casson joins as head of North American mining investment banking in Toronto from Morgan Stanley, where he served as managing director of metals and mining for North America. Christopher Dahan joins as a managing director focused on natural-resources M&A in Houston, moving from Perella Weinberg’s TPH & Co., where he advised on energy and infrastructure transactions. Greg Kantrowitz joins as a managing director covering power, renewables and clean technology in New York. He previously led clean-energy transition coverage at Citigroup. The appointments expand JPMorgan’s capabilities across mining, energy-infrastructure M&A, power, renewables and clean technology, strengthening its coverage of resource-intensive industries and the broader energy transition. $JPM $MS $C

items.title: $NFLX Deutsche Bank flipped to Buy yesterday, from Hold, with the target trimmed to 95 from 100. Analyst Bryan Kraft's argument is geogr
items.content_excerpt: $NFLX Deutsche Bank flipped to Buy yesterday, from Hold, with the target trimmed to 95 from 100. Analyst Bryan Kraft's argument is geographic. The engagement debate has been fought on US Nielsen data (YouTube at a record 14.2% of TV time, Netflix at a multi-year low of 7.8%). Kraft says international engagement has grown year over year for four straight six-month periods, and more than 60% of Netflix's production now happens outside the US. The valuation part: about 18x his 2027 earnings estimate, down from roughly 40x forward in June 2025. He sees a re-rating into the low-to-mid 20s. Still down ~26% this year and 36% off the April high of 107.79. Wells Fargo went Underweight two weeks ago. Tracking this into the Oct 20 print.

$CAPR Capricor's late-breaking WMS poster has the number behind tonight's ~20% after-hours pop. Patients who switched from placebo to deramiocel in HOPE-3 slowed upper-limb decline 76% vs their own prior year on placebo (PUL 2.0 scale: 2.05 points down to 0.49). Elbow-related function slowed 66% (1.33 to 0.45). Same patients, two different years: year 1 on placebo is the control for year 2 on drug. The group on drug from the start read almost identical across both years (0.95 vs 0.89 points). Both groups beat the natural-history model over two years (3.42 vs 5.88 predicted for the early group; 3.76 vs 5.35 for switchers). This data is already inside the BLA. Capricor filed the 24-month cut as a major amendment after July's adcomm, pushing the PDUFA to November 22. B. Riley is Buy / $21 PT (from $5) with a 40% approval probability. Stock closed at $8.57, down 70% YTD. Saturday's follow-up WMS presentation covers muscle and cardiac efficacy.

$VNDA Vanda's Phase III readout for Hetlioz in delayed sleep-wake phase disorder hit this morning: sleep onset moved 42.5 minutes earlier on drug vs 5.4 on placebo, a 37.1-minute difference (p=0.022). Responder rate: 60% advanced at least 30 minutes vs 15% on placebo. This is a label expansion, not a new molecule, which matters for two reasons. One: the sNDA rides on an already-approved drug with a known safety profile. Two: the population math. Hetlioz's current indications are rare ones. Vanda puts DSWPD prevalence at 0.5 to 4.1 million US adults. If approved, it would be the first FDA-approved medicine for the condition. Keep the small print in view: 43 patients enrolled over five-plus years, 40 in the efficacy analysis, and the endpoint was a sleep diary. Vanda will discuss the data with FDA before filing the sNDA.

stocks.summary: Deutsche Banks upgrade of Netflix to Buy after a steep selloff is drawing attention, with its bullish case emphasizing international engagement and valuation despite concerns about weaker U.S. viewing. Traders are split between seeing the upgrade as a buying opportunity and expecting continued pressure amid analyst downgrades, YouTube competition, and questions about Netflixs content slate.

messages.body: $NFLX
$NFLX
$NFLX i really hope you bought the dip

$NFLX Deutsche Bank flipped to Buy yesterday, from Hold, with the target trimmed to 95 from 100. Analyst Bryan Kraft's argument is geographic. The engagement debate has been fought on US Nielsen data (YouTube at a record 14.2% of TV time, Netflix at a multi-year low of 7.8%). Kraft says international engagement has grown year over year for four straight six-month periods, and more than 60% of Netflix's production now happens outside the US. The valuation part: about 18x his 2027 earnings estimate, down from roughly 40x forward in June 2025. He sees a re-rating into the low-to-mid 20s. Still down ~26% this year and 36% off the April high of 107.79. Wells Fargo went Underweight two weeks ago. Tracking this into the Oct 20 print.

Investors have been focused on weaker U.S. engagement, but international viewing minutes reportedly grew 5.4% while U.S. viewing fell 8.6%. And more than 60% of Netflix content produced since 2024 has been international. Netflix is a global business. That matters a lot more than one weak engagement datapoint in the U.S.
